phase_name: PCAE v0.3 Release Strategy and Capability Prioritization Reassessment
phase_title: PCAE v0.3 Release Strategy and Capability Prioritization Reassessment
recommended_next_phase: Begin the v0.3 core-adoption 'Must Have' work item: a concrete, documented integration point where PCAE observes or gates an actual AI coding agent's session on a real repository, using existing capabilities (pcae agent verify-handoff, context, execution-snapshot) rather than new execution machinery. HATP/HMIC/Remote WebAuthn continues as a decoupled Enterprise Security Extension track and is not blocking.
summary: Analysis and decision-only phase (no implementation, no production source changes, no HATP activation, no FIDO2 enrollment, no WebAuthn infrastructure deployment, no DNS/TLS provisioning, no RP-ID selection, no release creation). Inspected actual GitHub releases (v0.1.0-rc1, v0.2.0), tags, and CHANGELOG rather than treating v0.1/v0.2 as future roadmap items. Section 1 documents what v0.1 and v0.2 actually delivered. Section 2 produces a capability matrix across 14 capability areas (Governance kernel, Execution boundary, Permission Broker, Runtime architecture, Repository Intelligence, Historical Memory, Context/Snapshot, Multi-agent orchestration, Plugin/adapter model, HATP, HMIC, FIDO2, Remote WebAuthn, Deployment governance), each classified Released / Candidate for v0.3 / Enterprise extension / Internal architecture / Future research, verified against live `pcae runtime inspect --json` output (runtime posture unchanged since v0.2.0: Observed, execution unavailable, 0 registered plugins) despite roughly 3,200 commits of phase work since v0.2.0. Section 3 defines the v0.3 product goal: close the gap between governing sessions in the abstract and governing a real agent session a user is actually running, via a five-minute, no-domain/no-TLS/no-hardware quick start. Section 4 explicitly recommends HATP/HMIC/Remote WebAuthn as an Enterprise Security Extension, decoupled from v0.3 core adoption, on the basis that a normal PCAE user should not need a domain, TLS infrastructure, FIDO2 hardware, or WebAuthn setup. Section 5 assesses competitive position (strengths: governance/auditability depth, explicit non-authorizing evidence boundary; weaknesses: zero live execution capability after two releases, documentation-to-code ratio, no first-time-user narrative). Section 6 proposes v0.3 scope (Must Have: real-agent-session integration point, five-minute quick-start, curated CLI surface; Should Have: Permission Broker consumption, Repository Intelligence surfacing; Enterprise Track: HATP/HMIC/WebAuthn/multi-agent orchestration; Deferred: live execution, REST API/dashboard). Section 7 gives a 90-day engineering/documentation/adoption/reference-deployment roadmap. Section 8 gives the final recommendation and reasoning, consistent with the project's own existing autonomy-roadmap doctrine that broader execution capability is a later maturity level requiring the current level proven safe first. Full document: docs/PHASE_149O_20L_7O_2P_V0_3_RELEASE_STRATEGY_AND_CAPABILITY_PRIORITIZATION_REASSESSMENT.md.
